name: Oxabolone

lead: Oxabolone is an anabolic steroid in the nandrolone family. People who discuss it in muscle-building circles associate it with lean mass gain and a fuller, more muscular physique.

As an anabolic-androgenic steroid it is classed as an androgen receptor agonist, the signalling that drives greater muscle protein synthesis. The parent compound was never sold as a drug, though an injectable ester, oxabolone cipionate, has seen medical use. Almost nothing has been published on it, and no trials of its effects on muscle or appearance were found.

paras: In physique discussions it is treated as one of the lesser-known compounds in the nandrolone class, used within muscle-gain phases alongside heavy training and a calorie surplus. Specific routines are not well documented in published sources.

Oxabolone is on the WADA prohibited list, so it is banned in most major sports. A 1995 case report described mucosal hyperpigmentation associated with it, and no broader safety data have been published. Anabolic steroids as a class are controlled substances in many countries.

angle.text: Oxabolone is a nandrolone-family anabolic steroid that users associate with lean mass gain. The route is anabolic steroid signalling, which drives greater muscle protein synthesis and more muscle mass. Very little has been published on it specifically.

lead: Oxabolone (4-hydroxy-19-nortestosterone) is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid in the nandrolone (19-nortestosterone) group.[1] Compounds in this class are used by some bodybuilders for the muscle size and leaner physique they associate with anabolic steroids, and oxabolone is discussed in that context, mostly as a rare or hard-to-find member of the family.[2][3]

The parent compound was never marketed itself; its cipionate ester, oxabolone cipionate, has been marketed for medical use as an intramuscular injection.[1] T Nation forum posts describe it under the older brand name Steranabol and list oxabolone cipionate in brand tables of injectable steroids.[4][5]

Oxabolone is on the World Anti-Doping Agency's list of prohibited substances and is banned in most major sports; anti-doping and workplace urine-screening panels reproduced in forum threads list it and its metabolite.[1][6][7] Published literature is sparse. No clinical trials of its muscle or appearance effects were located; the only indexed human report concerns a skin and mucosal side effect.[8]

paras: Oxabolone is a 19-nortestosterone derivative carrying a hydroxyl group at the 4-position.[1] Related compounds include its 17-alpha-methylated analogue methylhydroxynandrolone and a further methylated derivative, oxymesterone.[1]

Oxabolone is listed among substances prohibited in sport by the World Anti-Doping Agency, and encyclopedic sources describe no mainstream therapeutic use of the parent compound.[1] Forum threads show it on lists of banned or screened steroids, including a thread on natural bodybuilding contest rules and one on an overseas job urine test.[6][7]

In T Nation threads, users have described oxabolone as a compound they would like to see available: a 2006 poster wished someone would make oxabolone cypionate, and a 2020 poster hoped for oxabolone and stenbolone to become available, saying they had read an account of oxabolone from the 1980s.[2][3] A 2002 poster said a supplement called Testobol had the same chemical structure as oxabolone, which they said had been manufactured as Steranabol, and suggested the product might be breaking rules.[5] These are user statements and were not verified.
A 1995 case report in Acta Dermato-Venereologica described mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone.[8] Beyond this report, no systematic safety data were located.
No studies found. The only human literature identified is the single case report of mucosal hyperpigmentation.[8]

lore.intro: On T Nation, oxabolone appears mainly as a rarely available nandrolone-class steroid that members mention wishing to see, and in lists of banned substances.[2][3][6]

claims.claim: Oxabolone is a desirable, hard-to-find nandrolone-type steroid.
A supplement product matched oxabolone's chemical structure.

timeline.event: Case report of mucosal hyperpigmentation attributed to oxabolone is published.[8]
